content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to figure out how to connect modules using the [product_name] configuration software. The manual explains that connections in the same network can be created by dragging a connector from one module to another, which results in a blue line. Selected lines are blue, while blue and green lines can be adjusted. When starting a new network project, I linked Module_1 to Module_2 as recommended and saw a blue line appear. Clicking the line set Module_1 as Client and Module_2 as Server. I then tested dependency programming between the modules, which resulted in a gray line; the source acted as Server and the target as Client, which seems logical since Module_2 operates based on Module_1's request. I haven't conducted a physical test and haven't changed addresses. My questions are: 1. Do you need to manually create a link line before programming if it can be generated automatically? 2. Will the presence of both blue and gray links cause any conflict? 3. What does the gray line indicate—will it change after physical connections and communication checks? 4. Aside from removing the connection, what options are available with the green line?

For your first question, you don't need to manually create a connection between two modules—the software does this automatically when you link an input in one diagram to an output in another. I've attached a helpful video on this. As for the second question, clicking a gray connecting line changes its color to blue to indicate selection. This doesn't cause a conflict; it just means you've set up two connections between your modules. Regarding the third point, the green connecting line simply represents the underlying physical Ethernet network and doesn't provide any extra configuration options.
Hi [user_name], This FAQ might help you—there are screenshots and an example project with two modules demonstrating how to monitor a connection between them. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are seeking guidance on connecting two modules within a network project using the configuration software, especially regarding the distinction between automatic and manual Ethernet connection creation and the significance of interface line colors. Topics of interest include interpreting visual cues and understanding configuration possibilities within the software, with some confusion about when connections are essential and how different mode settings impact network setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward advice on whether manual link creation is necessary, what the different colored lines represent in the interface, and clarification on which steps are automated by the software versus those requiring user input.
